title: wikiHow sues OpenAI over ChatGPT's use of its how-to articles
reason: Published: wikiHow, Inc. filed a copyright/DMCA lawsuit against OpenAI, Inc. and eight affiliated entities in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York on 21 August 2026 (case no. 1:2026cv07171). Fresh verifier and fresh adversarial falsifier run independently and in parallel; both converged on the same docket, filing date, and complaint figures with no disagreement. The filing itself is confirmed via named-byline Reuters reporting (Blake Brittain) plus independently-read writeups from IPWatchdog and MediaNama and a Justia/CourtListener docket record. The substantive infringement allegations (training-data scraping, runtime RAG reproduction, CMI stripping, visit/crawl figures, licensing-approach narrative) are wikiHow's own pleaded claims from the complaint -- tagged single-source and attributed throughout, per verification.md's legal-claim standard, never stated as fact. Two of the four originally-surfaced leads (ababnews.com, Digital Music News) could not be located by either sub-agent despite repeated search attempts and were dropped from sourcing entirely -- not cited anywhere. No OpenAI comment found as of publication. dedup-check returned one moderate match against delhi-hc-ani-openai-copyright-ruling; read and confirmed unrelated (different jurisdiction, plaintiff, court and procedural stage) -- published standalone.
